own_solution.law: At constant voltage F = (1/2) V^2 dC/dx with C(x) = C0[1 + (kappa - 1) x/L], so F = (1/2) V^2 C0 (kappa - 1)/L
assumptions: slab fills the gap thickness and width
slab edge well away from plate ends so force independent of x

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: TE652 and TBFE0 add a 350 V battery 'in series with the battery' without saying which way it faces, so the emf could be 850 V (F = 2.17 mN) or 150 V (F = 0.0675 mN).

counterexamples: TE652 with the extra battery opposing: V = 150 V, F = 0.5 x 22500 x 6e-9 = 6.75e-5 N = 0.0675 mN instead of 2.1675 mN.
notes: dC/dx = 200 pF x 3 / 0.10 m = 6e-9 F/m; F = 0.5 x 500^2 x 6e-9 = 7.5e-4 N = 0.75 mN. Aiding 350 V: 850 V gives 0.5 x 722500 x 6e-9 = 2.1675e-3 N. The insertion depth (4.5 cm of 10 cm) enters C(x) but cancels from dC/dx; it could also be read as K (force independent of x only while the slab's edge is away from the plate ends, and 4.5 cm is inside that regime). Numeral-free sentences T9C5B and T8F88 lack the 350 V of their counterparts.
